CHAPTER 01 / WEEK 01

FIRST TAKE: OPENING SUNDAY

The division races begin here. Three matchups, three very different reasons to watch, and no easy answers on the opening weekend.

● LIVE
ESPN FIRST TAKE | SUNDAY KICKOFF SPECIAL9:00 AM ET | Shae Cornette, Stephen A. Smith, Ryan Clark, Dan Orlovsky, Marcus Spears
NEW YORK
Shae Cornette (welcoming)

Good morning, everybody. Football is back. We have Baltimore traveling to Cleveland, Green Bay visiting Chicago, and Tennessee opening against Atlanta. Three games that could tell us an awful lot about where these teams are headed. Stephen A., where do you want to start?

Stephen A. Smith (energized)

Baltimore. Because I want to see Caleb Williams take command of this football team. The Ravens did not put all those pieces around him to play conservative football. You go into Cleveland, in your own division, and you make a statement.

Marcus Spears (leaning forward)

Hold on. Cleveland has a say in that, too. You want to talk about the Ravens offense, I want to talk about how Cleveland gets Caleb off his spot. If he is comfortable, you're in for a long afternoon. If they make him hold the ball, that changes the whole ballgame.

Dan Orlovsky (analytical)

For Baltimore, the first question is whether Caleb can stay efficient without forcing explosives. The passing game has enough talent. Alec Pierce stretches the field, Rashod Bateman can work underneath, Mark Andrews gives him a reliable middle target. The protection and decision making are what I'll be watching.

Ryan Clark (agreeing)

And do not overlook the other side. The Browns need a running game. If Cleveland can't run the football, Baltimore's defense is going to tee off on that quarterback. Then the whole day becomes about surviving third down.

Shae Cornette (curious)

You mentioned Baltimore's weapons. The Ravens spent quite a bit of draft capital to move up to fifth overall. What does Nasir Cruz actually add to this group?

Dan Orlovsky (explaining)

Versatility. His route releases look almost identical, and he can create separation in a small area. But what interests me most is whether Baltimore lets him play all over the formation. If he is just parked outside and told to win go routes, that's missing the point of the pick.

Stephen A. Smith (challenging)

I understand the tape, Dan. I do. But nobody gets a trophy for a pretty release. They traded their original first, their second, and next year's first to go get him. Caleb needs somebody to help move the chains. That is how I am judging that investment.

Ryan Clark (measured)

And the kid doesn't have to be the entire offense on day one. He should be dangerous because defenses have to respect everybody else. That's when a clever route runner can really hurt you.

Shae Cornette (transitioning)

Let's move to Chicago. The Bears are favored at home against Green Bay. And look at the quarterback matchup. Lamar Jackson for Chicago, and Ryan Miller for the Packers because Kyler Murray is sidelined with a high ankle sprain.

Stephen A. Smith (skeptical)

Now that is a problem! You have Lamar Jackson, who can wreck your defensive plan with his legs, and across the field you have a rookie who was supposed to spend the fall holding a clipboard. Green Bay better have a tremendous plan.

Marcus Spears (firm)

The Packers plan has a name. Jahmyr Gibbs. If Green Bay is smart, the first fifteen plays tell that young quarterback he doesn't have to be Superman. Hand it off, get a manageable third down, throw the easy completion. Keep Lamar watching from the sideline.

Dan Orlovsky (focused)

And here's where the Penn State background matters. Ryan Miller wasn't drafted because he threw fifty passes a Saturday and carried a program on his back. He was drafted because he could manage an offense, use play action, and usually avoid disastrous decisions. That's the job description right now.

Ryan Clark (skeptical)

That works in theory. But when you line up across from Lamar Jackson, the scoreboard can make a quarterback rush. If Chicago gets seven early, can Miller remain patient, or does he start trying to make throws he isn't supposed to make?

Stephen A. Smith (pointing)

Exactly! I am not asking a third round pick to throw for four hundred yards. I am asking him not to hand Chicago possessions. There is a difference between being a game manager and letting the game manage YOU.

Shae Cornette (inquiring)

So if Green Bay wins, who gets the credit?

Marcus Spears (confident)

If they win this kind of game, you're probably talking about the offensive line, Gibbs, and the defense. That's not a knock on the kid. That's the sensible way to win while your starting quarterback is hurt.

Dan Orlovsky (adding)

And his first completed pass matters. People overlook that. Get him an easy throw early, let him settle, then see if he can make the second and third reads. He is not being asked to take Kyler's job permanently.

Shae Cornette (pivoting)

Last stop, Atlanta. Tennessee made some big decisions this offseason. Jaxson Dart is leading this offense, A.J. Brown is still capable of taking over games, and Myles Garrett headlines that defense. Is this team better than people think?

Marcus Spears (animated)

I'm watching Garrett! Because when you have a defensive lineman who can disrupt the pocket without a blitz, everybody behind him plays faster. That's how you protect a young secondary. Atlanta needs to get the ball out, or that pass rush is going to ruin their afternoon.

Stephen A. Smith (considering)

I want to know what Tennessee is offensively. Jaxson Dart has the talent, A.J. Brown is a grown man out there, but you're not going to win every Sunday just throwing to one guy. They need balance and they need to finish drives.

Ryan Clark (analytical)

And they made a bold call at corner. Lachlan Knox, the Oregon rookie, is listed ahead of some established names, including Quinyon Mitchell and Charvarius Ward. A corner taken fifteenth overall needs to play, but number one on the depth chart is a lot of responsibility in your first game.

Shae Cornette (probing)

There have been questions about whether Ward is happy with that arrangement. We haven't heard him publicly confirm that. How much does it matter in a veteran locker room?

Ryan Clark (direct)

You have to manage it. A veteran isn't always going to love seeing a rookie take the first assignment. But it's not a popularity contest. The coaches should play the guy they think gives them the best chance. Then everybody has to handle it professionally.

Dan Orlovsky (thoughtful)

And coverage stats alone might not tell the whole story. If Atlanta consistently looks away from Knox, he won't have ten tackles or two interceptions. That doesn't mean he played badly. It means we need the tape before we declare success or failure.

Stephen A. Smith (emphatic)

Right. Stop putting him in the Hall of Fame before he plays a down, and stop calling it disrespect to the veterans before we see what he can do! Tennessee needs to beat Atlanta. That's the headline.

Shae Cornette (upbeat)

We've talked matchups, quarterback pressure, offensive identity, and personnel decisions. Now put the odds on the screen. Who's actually going to win?

CHAPTER 03 / WEEK 01

THE BALTIMORE EXPLOSION

A debut that stopped being a normal football game.

BALTIMORE RAVENS | ROAD OPENER

44 TO 7.
18 CATCHES.
FIVE TOTAL SCORES.

It was supposed to be an early test of whether the fifth overall pick could handle NFL coverage. Instead, Nasir Cruz spent his first Sunday rewriting the rookie record book.

18RECEPTIONS
135REC YARDS
5TOTAL TD

Baltimore scored fourteen points in the first quarter, seven in the second, sixteen in the third, and seven in the fourth. Cleveland did not reach the end zone until the final period. The final margin was thirty seven points, but the biggest story was how often the Ravens put the ball in their rookie receiver’s hands.

Cruz caught 18 passes for 135 yards and four touchdowns, with 102 yards after the catch. He also took five carries for 44 yards and a rushing touchdown. He accounted for five of Baltimore’s touchdowns and demonstrated why the team wanted him operating everywhere in the offense, not merely running conventional wide receiver routes.

Caleb Williams completed 28 of 38 passes for 296 yards and five passing touchdowns, though his two interceptions are an obvious correction point. Alec Pierce caught three passes for 62 yards and a touchdown. Romeo Doubs added four catches for 62 yards. Cleveland’s J. Storm threw four interceptions as the Browns managed only 134 offensive yards.

NEW ROOKIE SINGLE GAME RECORD | MADDEN UNIVERSE18
RECEPTIONS

Cruz passes the real world rookie benchmark of 15, set by Puka Nacua in 2023. He finishes three short of the franchise’s overall single game record of 21.

Kevin Burkhardt (in disbelief)

You are looking at a rookie who has caught eighteen footballs in his very first NFL game. Eighteen. And they are still finding ways to hand it to him.

Tom Brady (studying replay)

What I notice is the spacing. The defender is leaning toward the route he thinks is coming, and Cruz is already cutting somewhere else. That hesitation is everything. When you get that kind of separation, the quarterback does not need to be perfect.

Kevin Burkhardt (amazed)

And he has four receiving touchdowns, one rushing touchdown. Baltimore traded up for a difference maker. Today he was the difference maker.

Baltimore Postgame Press Conference

BALTIMORE PRESS ROOM

“I WASN’T COUNTING.”

Baltimore beat reporter (astonished)

Eighteen receptions. Puka Nacua had the rookie single game record at fifteen, and you passed him in your very first game. At what point did you realize the record was yours?

Nasir Cruz (grinning)

I honestly had no idea until somebody on the sideline told me. I was more worried about the next play. Then they said eighteen and I thought, alright, that is a nice start. But do not tell me the old record was fifteen like I was supposed to stop there.

ESPN reporter (following up)

You finished only three catches shy of the NFL record of twenty one. If somebody had told you in the fourth quarter, would you have wanted Caleb to keep feeding you?

Nasir Cruz (laughing)

You are asking a receiver if he wants the ball? Of course I do. But you have to respect the scoreboard. We had already done our job, so I can live with eighteen tonight. Ask me again if I get that close in a tight game.

NFL Network reporter (curious)

Four receiving touchdowns, another one rushing. That is five touchdowns from two completely different roles. Were you surprised how much Baltimore put on your plate immediately?

Nasir Cruz (animated)

That is why I liked coming here. They did not draft me to stand on one side of the formation and run three routes. I have been in the slot, outside, moving around, coming across the backfield. Different starting points, same problem for a defense. Find seventeen before seventeen finds space.

Cleveland reporter (probing)

On that early touchdown near the sideline, the defender was chasing you right toward the boundary. What did you see as you broke free and got into the end zone?

Nasir Cruz (smirking)

His hips. I could tell where he wanted me to go, and I gave him a little bit of that picture. Once he committed, I had the angle. Caleb got it there and I just had to finish. Being close to the sideline does not mean I am out of room.

Fox Sports reporter (curious)

You came out of Project APEX, where you trained alongside Lachlan Knox, who had his own debut with Tennessee today. Did you hear from him after this game?

Nasir Cruz (laughing)

Not yet. He is probably thinking of something annoying to say about all those short catches. That is Lockie. I saw Tennessee won, so good for him. But do not turn his season into a footnote in mine. He has been a serious corner since we were kids.

What do you think the rest of the league sees on this tape? A spectacular opening day, or a blueprint for how to defend you next week?

CHAPTER 04 / WEEK 01

GREEN BAY SURVIVES

One rookie gets a headline. Another gets a lesson.

GREEN BAY PACKERS | AT CHICAGO

A WIN THAT
DOES NOT FEEL
LIKE ONE.

Green Bay leaves Chicago 1 and 0. Ryan Miller leaves with a quarterback rating of 21.3 and plenty to answer for.

80PASS YARDS
4/13COMP / ATT
0/1TD / INT

The Bears led 13 to 10 at halftime. Neither team scored in the third quarter. Green Bay needed nine fourth quarter points and a defense that kept Chicago to three to escape with a 19 to 16 victory.

Miller’s passing numbers were rough: 4 completions on 13 attempts, 80 yards, zero touchdowns, one interception, four sacks. He scrambled four times for 25 yards. Chicago quarterback Lamar Jackson threw for 284 yards and a touchdown on 12 of 18 passing, but was sacked eight times. The Packers' defense made every possession a struggle.

Jahmyr Gibbs was the lifeline: 12 carries, 158 yards, one touchdown, including an 82 yard run. That is 13.2 yards per carry. Miller did not have to rescue the Packers because Gibbs and the defense kept them alive long enough to steal the fourth quarter.

Ian Eagle (calling the finish)

Green Bay has done just enough. The Packers win this game nineteen to sixteen, and you can see the relief on that sideline.

Charles Davis (concerned)

But when you are evaluating Ryan Miller, you cannot let the win hide the performance. Four completions. Thirteen throws. Four sacks. There is a lot of work to do.

Ian Eagle (reflective)

And yet, for a rookie who did not expect to start Week One, he gets to go home with a victory. That matters too.

POSTGAME MEDIA | WEEK 01

Green Bay Postgame Press Conference

GREEN BAY PRESS ROOM

“I HAVE TO BE BETTER.”

Green Bay beat reporter (direct)

Ryan, the Packers won nineteen to sixteen, but you completed four of thirteen passes for eighty yards with an interception. How do you describe your first NFL start?

Ryan Miller (visibly frustrated)

A win for the team and a bad day for me. That is the cleanest way to put it. We did enough to finish the game ahead, but I made it much harder on everybody than it needed to be.

ESPN reporter (probing)

Your passer rating was twenty one point three. You came out of Penn State with a reputation for making the safe, efficient decision. What broke down?

Ryan Miller (measured)

I was not efficient tonight. I rushed a few reads, held the ball on others, and the timing was not where it had to be. I do not want to blame the first start or the crowd. I have practiced those situations. I have to execute them.

Chicago reporter (specific)

You were sacked four times. Was that the protection, the coverage, or your hesitation as you tried to process Chicago’s looks?

Ryan Miller (accountable)

All of it shows up on film, but I know there are sacks I can help prevent by getting us into the right answer sooner. Our line fought. I cannot stand here and make it sound like four sacks are just something that happened to me.

Green Bay beat reporter (pressing)

You had an interception and no passing touchdowns. What would you say to your defense, which gave you chance after chance to win this game?

Ryan Miller (quietly)

Thank you, and I owe them a cleaner game. When the defense keeps you in it, you have to protect the ball. I did not do that well enough. They should expect better than what I gave them.

NFL Network reporter (curious)

Green Bay scored ten in the first quarter and then went quiet through the next two. Were you trying too hard to avoid a mistake once Chicago adjusted?

Ryan Miller (thinking)

I think I got too careful at times and then too impatient trying to make up for it. That is a bad combination. I need to take the simple throw when it is there, but I cannot freeze when it is not. We lost our rhythm, and I have to help us find it again.

Green Bay reporter (inquiring)

Jahmyr Gibbs ran for a hundred fifty eight yards on just twelve carries, including an eighty two yard burst and a touchdown. Does it bother you that everyone is going to say he carried the offense?

Ryan Miller (firm)

No. He did carry us in a lot of ways. That is not an insult to me, that is what happened. Jahmyr was incredible. My responsibility is to make sure teams cannot load up to stop him because they do not respect our passing game.

Fox Sports reporter (analytical)

You also ran four times for twenty five yards. With your mobility and your size, did you ever consider taking off more instead of forcing throws?

Ryan Miller (thoughtful)

There were chances. A few times I made the right decision to run, a few times I probably should have made it earlier. But I cannot turn every passing concept into a scramble because I am uncomfortable. My eyes have to stay where the play is supposed to go first.

Chicago beat reporter (challenging)

Lamar Jackson threw for two hundred eighty four yards on the other side, and Chicago was threatening until the end. Did watching him work affect how you approached your own possessions?

Ryan Miller (honest)

You know who is on the other sideline. But if I start trying to match Lamar Jackson throw for throw, I am already doing the wrong thing. He is one of the best. My job was to run our offense, and tonight I did not do that consistently.

ESPN reporter (following up)

The Packers defense sacked Jackson eight times and kept you close enough to come back. Is there a risk this win hides just how far you have to go?

Ryan Miller (serious)

There is no hiding it in our building. Coaches are going to put every snap on the screen. I know what the numbers look like. The win matters, but if I play like that every week, we will not win many.

Green Bay beat reporter (curious)

When Kyler Murray went down with the high ankle sprain, the plan to let you develop quietly was over almost immediately. What did he tell you before your debut?

Ryan Miller (softly)

He told me not to try to win the whole game on one snap. He has been good to me since I got here. I probably did not follow that advice every time. We will look at the tape together and I will listen.

NFL Network reporter (probing)

Do you feel pressure to prove that a third round quarterback who is five foot eleven belongs as a starter, especially after this first performance?

Ryan Miller (reserved)

I did not get drafted to win an argument about my height. They saw something they wanted to develop. Right now I have to earn the trust of the people in that locker room. That is harder and more important than winning a debate outside it.

Green Bay reporter (careful)

There was at least one thirty yard completion that showed you can hit an explosive pass. How do you create more of those without turning the ball over?

Ryan Miller (focused)

By being on time. One good throw does not fix the rest of the night, but it shows what we can do when I see it clearly and trust my feet. I need to make those decisions more often and stop putting the offense behind the chains.

ESPN reporter (direct)

Do you want to be the starter when Murray is healthy again?

Ryan Miller (straight faced)

I want to be good enough that the coaches trust me whenever my number is called. Kyler is our quarterback and he is hurt. I am not going to turn his injury into some competition I announce at a microphone. I just need to play better next week.

Green Bay beat reporter (final)

Was there anything you enjoyed about your NFL debut?

Ryan Miller (faint smile)

Winning. That part was good. I would like to enjoy the film a little more next time.

CHAPTER 05 / WEEK 01

TENNESSEE TAKES CONTROL

The league knows his name. Tennessee opens with 447 offensive yards and a seven point victory.

TENNESSEE TITANS | ROOKIE WATCH

WELCOME
TO FORT
KNOX.

Named Tennessee’s opening day CB1, Lachlan Knox made three tackles in his NFL debut. He did not force a turnover or register a pass breakup, but the Titans’ defense held Atlanta scoreless in the fourth quarter to secure a 34 to 27 win.

3TOTAL TACKLES
2SOLO TACKLES
1ASSIST

Born in Melbourne, developed through Project APEX and the NFL Academy pathway, and drafted out of Oregon, Knox enters the league with unusual football roots and a clear defensive identity. His technique, nicknamed Deadbolt, is built around patience, leverage and refusing to give away a route before it develops.

The Titans also have Myles Garrett pressuring quarterbacks and Jaxson Dart leading the offense. Knox is entering a team that expects to compete, not simply give a rookie a developmental season. The question is whether he can turn physical gifts into reliable coverage against professional receivers.

Result status: the Titans versus Falcons final score, defensive box score and specific Knox plays have not been provided in the available screenshots. This page preserves the matchup and character coverage without fabricating a victory, interception or highlight.

Kevin Harlan (setting the scene)

A lot of attention on Tennessee’s young corner, Lachlan Knox. He has the speed. He has the confidence. Now he has to show that his press technique works on Sundays.

Trent Green (analytical)

And the important thing is not whether he gets an interception immediately. A corner can play an excellent game without ever being targeted. We need the coverage snaps before we hand out a grade.

GAME RECAP

THE SECOND HALF BELONGS TO TENNESSEE

Atlanta scored 17 in the opening quarter and briefly looked ready to dictate the pace. Tennessee trailed 17 to 7 before grinding the deficit down to three at halftime. By the end of the third quarter, the teams were level at 27. Then the Titans defense held Atlanta scoreless in the fourth while Tennessee found the winning touchdown.

For Knox, the first game was a lesson in what being a professional corner actually means. He finished with three tackles and no credited pass breakups. There was no interception to post on social media, no theatrical signature moment. There was a win, and a defense that delivered when the game was tied. On the other side of the ball, Dart threw 54 passes and Brown caught 10, giving the rookie corner a very different supporting cast from the one Ryan Miller had in Green Bay.

POSTGAME MEDIA | WEEK 01

Tennessee Postgame Press Conference

TENNESSEE PRESS ROOM

“MAKE THEM EARN IT.”

Tennessee beat reporter (upbeat)

Lachlan, Tennessee wins thirty four to twenty seven after falling behind seventeen to seven in the first quarter. What did you learn about this team in your debut?

Lachlan Knox (relaxed)

That nobody panicked. We had a rough start, no point dressing it up. But the sideline stayed together. You cannot get back ten points in a single defensive snap. You just have to keep giving the offense another chance.

ESPN reporter (probing)

You were named the starting number one corner ahead of established players, including Quinyon Mitchell and Charvarius Ward. Did that surprise you?

Lachlan Knox (confident)

The coaches told me my job, and I went to work. You do not walk into a room with those blokes and think you are entitled to anything. You have to earn it every day. That does not mean I am going to act surprised when I get a chance I have been working for.

Tennessee reporter (careful)

There have been outside questions about how veterans would receive a twenty one year old rookie at the top of the depth chart. Have you felt tension with Ward or anybody else?

Lachlan Knox (matter of fact)

You would have to ask them how they feel. I am not speaking for another man. In the meetings we all need the same thing, good communication and good coverage. Nobody wins because of an argument over what is written on a depth chart.

NFL Network reporter (analytical)

Atlanta managed only a hundred thirty passing yards and thirteen completions on thirty two attempts. How much of that was the secondary versus the pass rush?

Lachlan Knox (thoughtful)

It is always tied together. A corner can stay tight for a few seconds, but if the quarterback stands back there forever, nobody is perfect. The rush helped us and we tried to make the timing difficult. That is team defense, not one bloke taking credit.

Atlanta reporter (direct)

Your individual line was three tackles, two solo and one assist. No interception, no recorded pass breakup. Do you feel like it was a quiet game?

Lachlan Knox (slight smile)

Very quiet on the stat sheet. Fine by me. I do not need to jump a route just to make the highlights if it means leaving someone free. There is plenty I need to clean up, but I am happy to go home without having given a receiver a free run for a big play.

Tennessee reporter (pressing)

A corner with your speed could gamble for the ball. What keeps you disciplined when you think you have the route diagnosed?

Lachlan Knox (focused)

If you guess wrong at this level, the ball is behind you and everyone sees it. I would rather trust my feet, hold my leverage and arrive at the catch point properly. Sometimes the big play is making the quarterback throw somewhere else.

Fox Sports reporter (curious)

Atlanta ran for a hundred forty two yards. Is that something the defensive backs have to take personally too?

Lachlan Knox (serious)

Absolutely. If a run gets outside, we are part of the problem. We are not separate from the front seven. There were angles and fits we can improve. Winning does not erase the points they put up.

Tennessee beat reporter (following up)

You held Atlanta scoreless in the fourth quarter while the Titans scored ten to win it. What changed defensively in that last period?

Lachlan Knox (measured)

Better communication, sharper tackling and fewer wasted movements. That is what it felt like. We were not trying to be heroes. We needed stops. They came, and the offense finished the job.

ESPN reporter (curious)

Jaxson Dart threw for three hundred forty six yards and A.J. Brown had ten catches for a hundred twenty five. Did you feel some relief watching the offense answer every time?

Lachlan Knox (grinning)

A bit, yeah. I am not going to complain about an offense that puts up thirty four. But I would prefer we do not ask them to rescue us every Sunday. We want to make it easier on them than that.

NFL Network reporter (smiling)

Why does everyone call you Fort Knox already? Is that a nickname you are comfortable carrying before you have even played two NFL games?

Lachlan Knox (dryly)

It sounds expensive, does it not? Look, I did not give it to myself. If I start letting blokes run free, you can all stop saying it. Until then I suppose I will live with it.

Tennessee reporter (personal)

You grew up in Melbourne playing Australian rules football. Was there a moment today when you realized you had really arrived in the NFL?

Lachlan Knox (reflective)

First time I lined up and heard how loud it was, probably. Then the ball was snapped, and it felt normal again. I still have the same job I had as a kid. See the ball, understand the space, do not let the other bloke beat you.

ESPN reporter (interested)

Your old Project APEX teammate Nasir Cruz just broke the rookie reception record in Baltimore. What was your reaction?

Lachlan Knox (laughing)

Eighteen catches is ridiculous. I saw the number after our game. Knowing Nas, he is probably annoyed they did not throw to him twenty times more. I am happy for him. We have been competing a long time, and one Sunday does not finish either story.

Tennessee beat reporter (final)

What do you want people to remember about your first start when they watch the film tomorrow?

Lachlan Knox (firm)

That I belonged out there, and that I still have work to do. We are one and zero. That is a good place to begin.

CHAPTER 06 / WEEK 01

MONDAY MORNING FIRE

The final scores are official. Now the pregame predictions get tested against what actually happened.

● ON AIR
ESPN FIRST TAKE | MONDAY RECAPShae Cornette, Stephen A. Smith, Ryan Clark, Dan Orlovsky, Marcus Spears
DEBATE DESK
Shae Cornette (welcoming)

Welcome back. Three games we talked about on Sunday, three teams we thought we knew, and three very different endings. Baltimore beats Cleveland forty four to seven. Green Bay escapes Chicago nineteen to sixteen. Tennessee takes care of Atlanta thirty four to twenty seven. Stephen A., did you learn more about the winners or the losers?

Stephen A. Smith (emphatic)

I learned Cleveland has a serious problem! Four turnovers by that quarterback, twelve rushing yards as an offense, and Baltimore hanging forty four on you? You cannot win a football game like that. The Ravens handled their business.

Marcus Spears (agreeing)

And that is why the Browns score bothered me most. They weren't just beaten on a couple of explosive plays. They couldn't establish a ground game at all. When your quarterback has to stand there against a defense that knows you're throwing, that is a nightmare.

Dan Orlovsky (analytical)

And Caleb Williams deserves credit. Twenty eight completions on thirty eight attempts, two hundred ninety six yards and five touchdowns. The two interceptions are still on his film, so it's not a flawless performance, but you cannot ignore how decisive the passing attack looked.

Shae Cornette (curious)

Speaking of that passing attack, Nasir Cruz ended up with eighteen catches for one hundred thirty five yards and four receiving touchdowns, plus a rushing touchdown. Eighteen catches breaks the rookie single game record. Did anybody see this coming?

Ryan Clark (astonished)

Not eighteen! I said before kickoff I wanted to see him handle NFL leverage, but Baltimore gave Cleveland no comfortable matchup for him. Outside, inside, on the move, even out of the backfield. That is coaching and talent working together.

Stephen A. Smith (laughing)

I picked Baltimore to cover and even I didn't see THAT. Four receiving touchdowns and a rushing touchdown? We're talking about a kid who scored five times in his first professional game! But let's not act like Cleveland covered itself in glory defensively.

Dan Orlovsky (measured)

The numbers are extraordinary. It's also just one game. Cleveland now gives every opponent a tape study of how Baltimore used him, and defenses will spend the entire week developing answers. The test comes when they adjust.

Shae Cornette (transitioning)

Now Green Bay. Marcus, you picked the Packers with the points, and they won outright. Dan, you picked Chicago to win a low scoring game. Well, it was low scoring, but Lamar Jackson and the Bears lost.

Marcus Spears (smiling)

Because Green Bay's defense showed up! Eight sacks against Lamar Jackson. That's the number that jumps off the screen to me. And Jahmyr Gibbs had a hundred fifty eight rushing yards on twelve carries, including that eighty two yard run. That's why I said this wasn't just about the rookie quarterback.

Stephen A. Smith (raising voice)

And thank goodness it wasn't! Ryan Miller completed FOUR passes. Four! One interception, four sacks, and a passer rating of twenty one point three. If Gibbs doesn't give you that explosive play, you're standing here explaining a loss.

Dan Orlovsky (serious)

I got the winner wrong. And I thought the defense might keep it close. But the quarterback tape is concerning. He had eighty passing yards, and the Packers had only sixty net passing yards because of the sacks. That cannot be a sustainable offensive formula.

Ryan Clark (firm)

I agree he played poorly, but I do not want a bust label thrown at him after one start. His job was supposed to be learning behind Kyler Murray, not opening against Lamar Jackson and Chicago. He still has to make the easy throws, but he gets a chance to respond next week.

Shae Cornette (probing)

And what about Lamar? Twelve completions on eighteen throws, two hundred eighty four passing yards and a touchdown. He also took eight sacks, and Chicago lost despite outgaining Green Bay.

Marcus Spears (critical)

That offense has to look at protection and situational football. You can't have that kind of explosive passing production and get beaten by a team that completes four throws. That's a team loss, not just a quarterback storyline.

Shae Cornette (pivoting)

Tennessee was the other favorite on our board. They cover the two and a half and win by seven. Jaxson Dart throws for three hundred forty six yards on fifty four attempts, A.J. Brown catches ten for one hundred twenty five, and the Titans finish with four hundred forty seven offensive yards.

Stephen A. Smith (approving)

Tennessee trailed twenty seven to twenty four entering the fourth quarter, then scored ten unanswered to win. That tells you as much about their finish as the final score does.

Ryan Clark (turning to defense)

And what I liked was the fourth quarter response. Atlanta didn't score again. Myles Garrett got a sack. The secondary didn't need one rookie to make every play. Lachlan Knox had three tackles with no interception or breakup, but that does not tell you he had a bad coverage game.

Marcus Spears (balanced)

Exactly. Quinyon Mitchell had two deflections, Ward was involved, and Knox did his job without a big stat line. If the staff named him the top corner, that's their decision. We will need a few weeks of tape before this becomes a referendum on who deserves the first assignment.

Stephen A. Smith (concluding)

Here is my bottom line. Baltimore looks dangerous, Green Bay looks resilient but has a real quarterback issue, and Tennessee has enough talent to win while that secondary finds its rhythm. That's football. It was never supposed to be three rookie auditions.

Shae Cornette (closing)

And next Sunday the questions get harder. Can Baltimore sustain this offense? Can Green Bay keep winning until Murray returns? Can Tennessee play from behind and finish? Week 1 gave us answers and even more questions.

Nightcap with Shannon Sharpe and Chad JohnsonLate Monday | Weekly reactions
THE FILM ROOM
Chad Johnson (animated)

Unc, I need you to look at this kid’s feet. Nasir Cruz is not just fast. Watch the stem. He sells the same thing every time. Corner got no clue which way he is going.

Shannon Sharpe (laughing)

Ocho, he caught eighteen passes. You do not need to convince me he can run routes.

Chad Johnson (insistent)

No, no, you missing it. He is making the defender commit before he commits. That is nasty. That is advanced stuff.

Shannon Sharpe (teasing)

You about to say he is better than you already?

Chad Johnson (grinning)

I did not say all that. But I would love to work out with him. I want to see if he can make me guess wrong.

Shannon Sharpe (thoughtful)

Now compare that to Ryan Miller. Completely different lesson. One kid has a coaching staff moving heaven and earth to get him touches. The other kid is trying to survive until his starter gets healthy.

Chad Johnson (nodding)

And that is why you cannot judge every rookie by the same box score. Nasir was the feature. Miller was the emergency plan.

Shannon Sharpe (closing)

But both wake up with a win. One is going to watch highlights. The other is going to watch corrections. Welcome to the NFL.

THE WEEK AFTER

What the results actually mean

THE BREAKOUT

Nasir: instant pressure

One historic game changes the conversation from potential to expectation. Defensive coordinators now have film of Baltimore moving Cruz all over the formation. Week Two will test the counters.

THE DEVELOPMENT

Miller: a narrow runway

He gets credit for surviving a divisional road game, but 4 of 13 passing cannot be the offensive plan. With Kyler Murray injured, his next start becomes an immediate evaluation.

THE DEFENDER

Knox: prove it on tape

The reputation is real. The verdict is not. Tennessee needs actual coverage data before fans or analysts can decide whether the rookie is a shutdown corner already.

AROUND THE LEAGUE | CROSS GAME DEBATE

THREE WINS, THREE DIFFERENT ROOKIE REPORT CARDS

Stephen A. Smith (emphatic)

Baltimore scored forty four, Tennessee scored thirty four, and Green Bay managed nineteen. Three victories, but do not tell me these rookies had the same Sunday. Cruz changed the game. Miller had to be rescued by his running game. Knox did not fill up the stat sheet, but his defense got a stop when it mattered.

Ryan Clark (analytical)

Exactly. We need to grade the assignment, not the social media clip. Knox has three tackles, no picks, no breakups. That does not prove he locked down everybody, and it does not prove he played poorly. The tape will tell us about his coverage snaps. What we do know is Atlanta got nothing in the fourth quarter.

Dan Orlovsky (explaining)

And look at the quarterback situations. Jaxson Dart completes thirty four balls for three hundred forty six yards. Ryan Miller completes four passes for eighty yards. Both teams won. That is why quarterback evaluation cannot stop at the final score. Green Bay has to find a more sustainable passing plan.

Shannon Sharpe (smiling)

And I want to see the rookie corner and the rookie receiver when they eventually line up across from one another. Cruz wants to disguise every route. Knox wants to sit on the release and not bite. That is a matchup worth circling when it comes around, but today both men got their first NFL win.
